wu: Warm-up: 'Stand if You Can' game. Teacher calls out sports (e.g., 'Run!'), students stand if they can do it. Teacher models: 'I can run.' Students repeat. Teacher calls 'Swim!', students sit if they can't. Teacher models: 'I can't swim.'
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Simon Says' with can/cant commands (e.g., 'Simon says: You can jump!')
Alternative 2: Quick survey: 'Ask 3 classmates: Can you play football?'. Tally results on board.
pres: Presentation: Show flashcards of sports (football, swim, run). Teacher models: 'I can play football.' Point to self. Then shows a sport they can't do (e.g., ice skate). Models: 'I can't ice skate.' Students repeat sentences chorally. Check: 'Can I play football?' (Yes!) 'Can I ice skate?' (No!)
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use a story about a character who can/can't do sports. Draw stick figures on board.
Alternative 2: Bring in a real football. Teacher demonstrates 'I can kick the ball.' Then tries to juggle and says 'I can't juggle.'
prac: Guided practice: 'Can-Can't Relay' in teams. Teams race to write sentences on board: 'I can swim.' 'I can't play tennis.' Teacher monitors for accuracy. Support: Give sentence starters on board.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Matching Pairs' worksheet. Match sports to can/cant sentences.
Alternative 2: 'Chain Drill'. Student 1: 'I can run.' Student 2: 'He can run. I can swim.'
ls: Listening slot: Students listen to 3 short interviews (audio recording) about sports. They complete a grid: 'Name / Can do / Can't do'. Check answers as class.
re: Reactivation game: 'Freeze Dance'. Play music, students dance. When music stops, teacher calls: 'Freeze! Can you jump?' Students jump if they can. If not, freeze.
prod: Production task: 'Talent Show Circle'. Students stand in a circle. Each student says: 'My name is [name]. I can [skill]. I can't [skill].' (e.g., 'I can sing. I can't dance.')
rw: Reading and writing slot: Students read 3 short ability profiles (e.g., 'Fatima: She can cook. She can't swim.'). They complete a grid with names and skills. Then write 3 sentences about themselves: 'I can... I can't...'
st: Story / song + goodbye: Sing 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' with can/cant twist (e.g., 'Can you touch your nose?'). Close with: 'Today we learned to say what we can and can't do. Thank you, class!'
g: Teams answer quiz questions: 'Who can swim? A) Ali B) Sara'
One student acts a sport, others guess: 'Can you play football?'
Student mimes a sport, others guess: 'Can you run?'
Students walk around asking: 'Can you play basketball?' and write names
Students write 9 abilities in grid. Teacher calls: 'Can you swim?' Students mark if they can.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 5 can/cant sentences about a famous athlete.
Support: Use picture prompts for writing sentences (e.g., a picture of a football for 'I can play football.')
hw: Option 1: Interview a family member: 'Can you cook? Can you drive?' Write 3 sentences.
Option 2: Draw 3 things you can do and 3 you can't. Label them in English.
Option 3: Complete the worksheet: 'My Sports Skills'.
tip: Use local sports like football and athletics to make it relevant. Encourage peer correction gently during the talent show to build confidence.
